summary: For ages 6–7: reading and writing numbers to at least 100 in words, extending from number words to twenty into the decade words (twenty, thirty … ninety) and two-word hyphenated compounds (fifty-seven). The central work is mapping word ↔ numeral ↔ quantity, learning commonly misspelled decade words (forty drops the u of four; ninety keeps the e of nine), fixing the hyphen, and untangling the sound-alike '-teen'/'-ty' pairs (fifteen/fifty, thirteen/thirty). Above twenty the English words follow a regular tens-first pattern (decade word, then ones word), a useful contrast with the teens, although some decade stems (twenty, thirty, fifty, forty) are spelled irregularly.
misconceptions: Confusing '-teen' and '-ty' words by sound and spelling (fifteen vs fifty, thirteen vs thirty).
Misspelling irregular decades (forty as 'fourty', ninety as 'ninty').
Omitting the hyphen or writing compounds as one/many words incorrectly.
Transposing compound numbers back to numerals (writing 'forty-two' as 24) — carrying over the teen ones-first habit.
Writing decade words with extra zeros from the spoken parts (fifty-seven → 507).

activities.title: Build compound number words from decade + ones parts
steps: Choose a decade-word part (e.g. 'sixty') and a ones-word part (e.g. 'four') and join them into the compound word 'sixty-four', writing it with the hyphen.

Write the numeral64 beside sixty-four and locate it on a0–100 line. Optionally join on-screen tens and ones word tiles so the compound immediately links to its numeral and line position, with a reverse round asking the learner to assemble or spell the word for83.
Work the reverse direction: shown the numeral 83, say and then correctly spell the word 'eighty-three'.
Write seventy-eight, seventy-nine, eighty, eighty-one, then ninety-nine and one hundred. Notice when a decade changes, when a hyphenated compound is used, and how100 is written.
activities.insight: For numbers from21 to99 with a nonzero ones digit, the English word is a tens-first compound, such as sixty-four. Exact tens use the decade word alone, and100 is one hundred; connect each form to its numeral and quantity.

activities.title: Sound-alike contrast: '-teen' versus '-ty'
steps: Take a minimal pair such as fifteen/fifty and read both aloud, stressing the ending (-teen vs -ty).
Beside each word, write its numeral (fifteen = 15, fifty = 50) and show a matching quantity or base-ten model (fifteen = 1 ten and 5 ones; fifty = 5 tens).
Repeat with thirteen/thirty and other pairs, each time pairing word, numeral and quantity so meaning separates the near-identical sounds.
Answer a quick 'fifteen or fifty?' decision with the set of objects visible, choosing by quantity rather than guessing.
activities.insight: The '-ty' word names a number of tens (fifty = 5 tens) while the '-teen' word is a teen (fifteen = 1 ten and 5); linking each to a quantity removes the guesswork from the near-identical sounds.

activities.title: Use number words in a real read-and-write task
steps: Given a label showing the numeral 76, write the words for a new label a customer could read ('seventy-six'), ordered correctly and hyphenated.
Given the word 'eighty-three' on a card, read it and write the numeral (83).
Check a friend's work: they wrote 803 for 'eighty-three' — decide whether it is right and explain what went wrong.
Compare 40 and 14 (and 'ninety' vs 'nineteen'): read each aloud and write each the other way to confirm you can move both directions.
activities.insight: A learner who has the system can move fluently in both directions — word to numeral and numeral to word — without concatenating the spoken parts or confusing teen and decade words.

checkQuestion: Give the child a real task: 'This sweet-jar label shows the numeral 76. Write the words for the new label so a customer can read it.' Then, separately: 'Your friend wrote the card and put the numeral for eighty-three — read the word and write the numeral.' Watch which words and numerals they actually produce and read aloud.
checkAnswer: Writes 'seventy-six' (decade word + ones word, correctly ordered and hyphenated) and writes 83 for 'eighty-three'.
